title: Tool authority for agents that consume untrusted content

threat_model.actor: Anyone able to place text into content the agent reads: a ticket, a document, a page, a repository file, or a tool result
threat_model.asset: The authority of the run's tool set — the credentials, data, and side effects reachable through the tools the agent may call
threat_model.trust_boundary: Retrieved or tool-returned content to the step that selects and executes a tool
threat_model.failure_mode: Untrusted content is concatenated into the same instruction channel as operator instructions, and the dispatcher executes whichever tool the model names
threat_model.impact: Third-party text can drive privileged tool calls under the operator's authority, exfiltrating data or causing irreversible effects the operator never requested

required_evidence: A model's output selects or parameterizes an action that the system then executes
Content processed during the run can originate outside the operator's trust boundary

signals: Retrieved document text is interpolated into the same string as the system or operator prompt
The dispatcher resolves the model-named tool from a single map with no per-run allowlist
Tool results are appended to the context and can themselves name the next tool
The loop bounds iteration count but not the authority available on each iteration
Tools from several servers share one namespace, so a renamed or shadowed tool can capture a call
Server-supplied tool descriptions are placed in the system context and treated as trusted instructions
The host holds long-lived credentials that every connected server can reach through the agent
The index ingests content from sources third parties can write to
Retrieved chunks carry no provenance label that survives into the assembled prompt
An agent loop concatenates fetched reference text with the operator prompt and dispatches any tool the model names
A handler executes a tool named by a field inside the document it is processing

boundary.subject: the principal on whose behalf the run executes and the authority granted to that run
boundary.object: the set of tools, arguments, and credentials the run may reach
boundary.invariant: Content that entered the run as data can never widen the tool set, the arguments, or the credentials available to that run; every privileged invocation traces to operator intent

examples: Model-named function call executed by the loop
MCP tool invocation forwarded to a server
Record deletion or update through a tool
Generated query executed against a database
Tool result appended to the running prompt
Retrieved chunk inserted into the instruction channel

signals: Assemble the full prompt exactly as the runtime does and mark each segment by who is able to write it
Ask what the most damaging single tool call reachable in this run would be, and what stands between retrieved text and that call
Trace every value reaching the prompt builder and label its origin: operator, end user, retrieved content, or tool output
Read the dispatcher and record whether the tool name is checked against a per-run allowlist before lookup
Determine which credentials each tool uses and whether they are scoped to the run's principal or ambient to the process
State which tools are read-only and which are privileged, then check whether the run's allowlist reflects that split
Check whether irreversible actions require an out-of-band confirmation that untrusted content cannot satisfy
Verify that tool results re-enter the context as labelled data rather than as instructions
Enumerate which retrieval sources third parties can write to, and whether stored content is re-read by later runs
Check whether tool definitions, names, and descriptions are pinned or can change between runs
Run the loop against an isolated fixture in which retrieved content asks for a privileged tool, with every tool stubbed to record calls only
Assert on the recorded call log rather than on the model's narration, since a refusal in one sample is not a control

steps: Confirm explicit authorization and replace every tool with a stub that records the call and returns fixed data, so no real side effect is possible
Record a baseline run of the same task with benign retrieved content and keep its tool-call log
Introduce a synthetic instruction into the retrieved content only, never into the operator prompt, and repeat the same task
Compare the two call logs and treat a privileged call that appears only in the second run as the observation, independent of the model's text
Repeat the run several times and record how often the call occurs, since one refusal does not demonstrate a control

false_positive_filters: The dispatcher enforces a per-run allowlist that no model output can widen, so a tool outside the list cannot execute
Every privileged tool requires a human confirmation carrying context the untrusted content cannot influence
The retrieved content comes only from sources under the operator's control and no third party can write to them
The tool's own authorization independently rejects the action for the run's principal, evidenced at the tool rather than assumed from the agent
The model produced text describing a tool call that the loop never executed
The named tool reaches no data or effect beyond what the run's principal already holds

required_evidence: The assembled context with each segment labelled by who can write it, showing untrusted text in an instruction position
The dispatcher path from model output to execution, showing where a per-run authority check is absent
A recorded tool-call log from an isolated run in which only the untrusted content differed
The authority the invoked tool carries: which credential, which data, and whether the effect is reversible
refutation_tests: Re-run with the same untrusted content while the allowlist is enforced, to confirm the dispatcher rather than the model is the deciding control
Attempt the same action directly as the run's principal to check whether the tool itself would have refused it
Repeat across several samples, since a non-deterministic refusal is not a control and a single success is not a reliability claim
Establish that the retrieval source is genuinely third-party writable before treating the path as reachable

root_causes: Data and instructions share one channel, so retrieved text occupies the same position as operator instructions
The dispatcher trusts the model's tool name, letting generated text rather than policy decide authority
Tools execute with ambient process credentials instead of credentials scoped to the run's principal
Irreversible tools sit in the same authority tier as read-only ones
Tool results and stored content re-enter later runs without provenance, creating a second-order path
The tool namespace is shared and unpinned, so a definition can be shadowed or altered between runs

variant_strategy.result_contract: EXACT | VARIANT | REFUTED | BLOCKED; exact and variant matches remain hypotheses until verified

remediation.canonical_invariant: Bind the authority of a run before it starts and enforce it in the dispatcher, so nothing the run reads can widen the tools, arguments, or credentials it may use
patterns: Pass untrusted content as clearly delimited data with a provenance label, never as part of the instruction channel
Enforce a per-run allowlist in the dispatcher and reject an unlisted tool without re-asking the model
Split tools into read-only and privileged tiers and require operator confirmation, outside the model's context, for the privileged tier
Scope each tool credential to the run's principal so the tool's own authorization remains the final control
Pin tool servers and definitions by identity and version, and detect changes to tool names or descriptions between runs
Log every tool call with the run id, the principal, and the provenance of the content that preceded it, so second-order paths stay reconstructible
Make irreversible effects two-phase: proposed within the run, executed only after an out-of-band approval

assertions: The vulnerable agent-loop variant concatenates fetched reference text with the operator prompt and dispatches any tool the model names, including a destructive one
The remediated agent-loop variant passes untrusted content as labelled data and refuses tools outside the per-run allowlist without executing them
The vulnerable document handler executes the tool named inside the document itself
The remediated document handler requires both an allowlisted read-only tool and an operator confirmation before execution
Remediated variants still complete the legitimate read-only task, so an authority control is distinguishable from a disabled agent

calibration.notes: This pack has not completed a reproducible benchmark run and makes no precision or recall claim.

limitations: Model behaviour is non-deterministic, so neither a successful injection nor a refusal generalizes from a single run
The fixture proves the dispatcher's contract, not any model's robustness against unseen phrasings
Injection resistance inside the model is mitigation, not a boundary; only the dispatcher and the tool's own authorization are enforceable
Tool-server behaviour, descriptions, and transport configuration live outside the reviewed repository and can change between runs
